page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core capabilities alongside constrained multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier single-core Geekbench scores in the top 10% and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression in the top 25%. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the bottom 10% and bottom 25% respectively, reflecting the low core count. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read and write speeds categorized in the bottom 10%.

The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for integer and tile operations. These hardware features assist in specific tasks like cryptography and lightweight machine learning inference, where it achieves average text generation speeds of 94.15 tokens per second on a small 135M model. Given the low memory capacity and lack of local storage, this server is best suited for single-threaded compute tasks, lightweight web serving, and basic utility workloads that benefit from dedicated CPU execution rather than memory-intensive operations.
